description: A group of students coming together to participate in NASA Space Apps, share ideas, and work on a project we're passionate about.
summary: Our project focuses on the challenges humans would face while exploring and surviving on Mars. We developed Red Horizon, an interactive educational website that uses real NASA data to explore Martian terrain, landing sites, and survival challenges. Our platform includes interactive maps of Jezero Crater and Olympus Mons, alongside a survival simulator based on the RIDGE framework: Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, and Environment. We also developed an Arduino-based environmental monitoring prototype designed to measure temperature and radiation levels and display the readings on an LCD screen. This demonstrates how sensors could help astronauts monitor potentially hazardous environmental conditions during future Mars missions. Our project's main impact is making complex NASA research more accessible and understandable, especially for students and young space enthusiasts. By transforming scientific data into interactive experiences and connecting it with practical engineering, we aim to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronauts while encouraging innovation in future space exploration.
details: Our project, Red Horizon is an interactive website designed to make Mars exploration and survival easier to understand. Built using Python, Django, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, it features interactive maps of Jezero Crater and Olympus Mons based on real NASA data. It also includes a survival simulator where users can adjust resources and environmental risks, alongside the RIDGE framework explaining five major challenges of human spaceflight. By combining scientific research, interactive simulations, and a futuristic design, our goal is to educate and inspire people about Mars exploration and future human missions.
